page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. A key hardware characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 35,433 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.d1.3xlarge delivers average multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8,789.97 and a PassMark CPU score of 10,074.03. However, single-core performance is weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,102.49 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.96 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed; while the uncached large-block read bandwidth is average at 54.9 GB/sec, the overall PassMark memory score is weak at 1,685.71. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, achieving 8.27 million operations per second on Redis.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.d1.3xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive local storage capacity without the premium cost of SSDs. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on slower HDD storage media and an older Intel Xeon CPU architecture, which limits single-threaded execution speed and high-speed web serving throughput. This instance is best suited for storage-intensive workloads, data archiving, large-scale log processing, and database applications that require high capacity over high random IOPS.
